behavior_constraints: --dedup-policy accepts exactly {first-arrival, lex-largest-ts}; unknown/empty value exits 2 with stderr line: ingest: --dedup-policy: must be one of {first-arrival, lex-largest-ts}
Omitting --dedup-policy or setting lex-largest-ts yields byte-for-byte identical output, rejects, state-out, audit-log, audit-log-digest, and manifest vs. prior round behavior
Under first-arrival, winner in a same-run duplicate group is the event with smallest (shard_basename, line_index); ts is not consulted
Cross-run dedup against state.seen_ids is unchanged by policy; cross_run duplicates remain unaffected
Rejects file still four-bucket layout in arrival order; duplicate bucket contains the non-winners under the active policy
anomalies.duplicate count unchanged between policies for same input

Audit log: same_run duplicate records under first-arrival carry winner_arrival={shard,line} immediately after reason; never emitted under lex-largest-ts/default; never on cross_run; never on non-duplicate buckets
Audit-log-digest duplicate_reasons still has exactly same_run and cross_run counts; winner_arrival is not surfaced in digest
When --audit-log-digest, --audit-log, and --dedup-policy are all set, digest gains dedup_policy_stats block positioned after resolved_against and before sha256
Flag composes freely with state, audit log, manifest, rates-strict, FX staleness flags
entities.summary: This round adds an optional --dedup-policy flag to eventq ingest selecting between the existing lex-largest-ts winner rule (default, byte-compatible) and a new first-arrival rule that picks the earliest (shard_basename, line_index) duplicate-group survivor, surfaces a winner_arrival object on same_run duplicate audit records only under first-arrival, and adds a dedup_policy_stats block to the audit-log digest when policy is set.

instruction_head:
# Configurable Dedup Policy

Same-run duplicate handling now has an explicit policy selector:
`--dedup-policy <first-arrival|lex-largest-ts>`. The default keeps the existing
winner rule: the lexicographically largest `ts` wins, with arrival order used
as the tie-breaker. The `first-arrival` policy deliberately chooses the event
with the smallest `(shard_basename, line_index)` in the duplicate group,
ignoring `ts` for winner selection.
